title: The EU Votes to Scan Private Messages
summary: The European Parliament approved a version of 'Chat Control,' a rule that would push messaging apps to scan the private chats and photos on your phone for illegal material before they are sent.

title: OpenAI Ships GPT-5.6
summary: OpenAI released GPT-5.

title: An AI Tutor That Answers a Child in One Second
summary: The team behind Ello, a reading app for young children, explained how they built an AI tutor that responds to a five-year-old in about a second — fast enough to feel like a real back-and-forth.

title: Running a Capable AI on an Ordinary Laptop
summary: A developer shared Colibri, a project for getting GLM 5.

title: How GitHub Gave Every Repository a Durable Owner
summary: GitHub found that of its 14,000-plus internal code repositories, fewer than half had a clear owner.

title: Making a Common AI Toolkit Run at Full Speed
summary: Hugging Face rebuilt the link between its widely used 'transformers' library — the default way most open AI models are written — and vLLM, a system for serving those models quickly.

title: An AI Produces a Proof That Eluded Mathematicians for 40 Years
summary: Previously covered on 2026-07-10: OpenAI released GPT-5.

title: Apple Sues OpenAI Over Alleged Trade-Secret Theft
summary: Apple has filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of taking confidential information through former Apple employees who moved to the AI company.

title: SpaceX Wants 100,000 More Starlink Satellites
summary: SpaceX has asked regulators for permission to launch roughly 100,000 additional Starlink satellites, which it says would multiply the network's total capacity about a hundredfold.

title: New York City Moves to Ban Sneaky Subscription Traps
summary: New York City passed rules cracking down on "deceptive subscription practices" — the hard-to-cancel sign-ups and hidden auto-renewals that quietly drain money each month.

title: A 15-Year-Old Flaw Found in Every Linux Distribution
summary: Researchers disclosed GhostLock, a memory-handling bug that has been present in essentially all Linux distributions for about 15 years.

title: Profiling PyTorch Attention, One Backend at a Time
summary: Hugging Face published the third part of a series on measuring where time actually goes inside a running AI model.

title: Why GitHub Made Its Copilot Code Reviewer Use Plain Unix Tools
summary: GitHub explained that adding fancy custom tools to its Copilot code-review agent actually made the reviews worse and more expensive.

title: The Money Behind the AI Boom Is Starting to Look Circular
summary: An investment analysis lays out how a small group of companies now fund each other's AI spending: Nvidia sells the chips that power AI, invests in cloud firms like CoreWeave and Nebius, and those firms then borrow and spend heavily to buy more Nvidia chips.

title: A Look at What Grok's Coding Tool Quietly Sends Back
summary: A developer inspected xAI's new Grok command-line coding tool and documented exactly what it transmits back to the company as you use it.

title: AI Voice Assistants Just Got Faster to Build
summary: Hugging Face and chipmaker Cerebras released a way to run Gemma 4, an open AI model, fast enough for real-time voice conversations.

title: A Free Tool That Tracks 15,000 Objects in Orbit
summary: A developer built Orbit, a browser-based augmented-reality tool that lets you point your phone at the sky and see the satellites and debris passing overhead — more than 15,000 tracked objects in all.

title: The Last American on an Iron Lung Has Died at 78
summary: Martha Lillard, believed to be the last person in the United States still relying on an iron lung to breathe, has died in Oklahoma.

title: Letting AI Keep Your Documentation in Sync — Across Repositories
summary: GitHub's Aspire team described how they use 'agentic workflows' — AI agents that run automatically when code changes — to turn each merged product update into a draft documentation update in a separate docs repository.

title: Running a Language Model Spread Across Several Machines
summary: A project called Mesh LLM shows how to run a large AI model split across several ordinary computers linked together over a peer-to-peer network, instead of on one big expensive server.

title: Your Browser's Math Can Now Reveal Which Computer You're Using
summary: Researchers found that since Chrome's latest Chromium update, a basic built-in math function returns slightly different results depending on your operating system, letting a website tell whether you're on Windows, Mac, or Linux — without ever asking.

title: A Real Team Moved to GPT-5.6 and Cut Its Costs by a Quarter
summary: Previously covered on 2026-07-10: OpenAI released GPT-5.

title: One of the Internet's Founders Is Retiring at Last
summary: Vint Cerf, widely called a 'father of the internet' for co-designing the basic rules that let computers talk to each other, is stepping back after decades at Google and across the industry.

title: Google Wants AI to Smooth Out Your Commute
summary: Google Research described a project that uses AI to fine-tune the timing of traffic lights, aiming to cut the stop-and-go congestion that wastes fuel and time.

title: How GitHub Cleared More Than 20,000 Security Alerts
summary: GitHub explained how it faced over 20,000 'secret scanning' alerts — automated warnings that a password or access key may have been accidentally saved into code — spread across 15,000 of its own repositories, and how it worked through every one to reach zero in nine months.

title: A New Test for AI That Modernizes Old Java Code
summary: IBM Research released ScarfBench, a benchmark that measures how well AI 'agents' can migrate large enterprise Java applications from one software framework to another — the kind of tedious, error-prone rewrite that big companies spend heavily on.

title: Japan Finds a Way to Reclaim Most of the Lithium in Dead EV Batteries
summary: Researchers in Japan demonstrated a process that recovers up to 90% of the lithium from spent electric-vehicle batteries, far more than most recycling methods manage today.

title: Telegram's Link Domain, t.me, Has Been Suspended
summary: The t.

title: California May Force Social Apps to Switch Off 'Infinite Scroll' for Teens
summary: A proposed California law would require platforms to disable engagement features like endless feeds and autoplay for users under 18.

title: A Rare Look at How Microsoft Gave Its Own Staff AI Coding Tools
summary: Researchers published a study of Microsoft's early-2026 rollout of two AI command-line coding assistants, Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI, to its developers.

title: One Place to Compare Uber, Lyft, Waymo, and Robotaxi Prices
summary: A new tool called Hackney lets you check the cost of the same trip across Uber, Lyft, Waymo, and other robotaxi services side by side.

title: How GitHub Made Its Issues Pages Feel Instant
summary: GitHub's engineering team rebuilt navigation for its Issues pages so moving between them feels immediate.

title: Someone Built a Neural Network Entirely in SQL
summary: A developer implemented a working neural network, the math behind modern AI, using nothing but SQL, the decades-old language designed for querying databases.

title: The AI Data-Center Boom Is Raising Your Electricity Bill
summary: A Fortune analysis found that the rapid build-out of data centers — much of it to power AI — has pushed roughly $23 billion in higher electricity costs onto ordinary utility customers, as grids strain to keep up with demand.

title: A Capable AI Model That Runs Entirely on Your Phone
summary: A team released Bonsai 27B, an AI model in the same size class as many cloud services that runs directly on a phone — no internet connection and nothing sent to a company's servers.

title: Microsoft Patches a Record 570 Security Flaws
summary: Microsoft's monthly security update fixed 570 vulnerabilities at once — the most it has ever addressed in a single batch.

title: A Flaw in Tailscale's Popular Networking Tool Allowed Root Access
summary: Tailscale, a widely used tool that lets companies connect their computers securely, disclosed a bug in its SSH feature that could have let an attacker gain full control of a machine.

title: AI Cracks 20 Long-Standing Math Problems at Once
summary: Researchers pointed 20 copies of OpenAI's Codex, running in parallel, at a famous list of unsolved problems posed by mathematician Paul Erdős — and reported solutions to 20 of them.

title: Dependabot Adds a Cooldown Before Adopting New Package Versions
summary: GitHub's Dependabot — the bot that automatically suggests updates to the third-party code libraries a project depends on — now waits a built-in 'cooldown' period before proposing a brand-new release, rather than pulling it in the moment it appears.

title: A Developer Trained an AI 'World Model' to Play Super Mario Bros.
summary: A developer built LeMario, a JEPA-style world model trained on Super Mario Bros.

title: Thinking Machines Releases Its First Open Model, Inkling
summary: Thinking Machines, the AI startup founded by OpenAI's former research lead Mira Murati, released Inkling — its first model with 'open weights,' meaning anyone can download it and run it on their own computers for free rather than renting access through a company's website.

title: xAI Opens Up the Code Behind Its Grok Coding Tool
summary: Elon Musk's xAI published the full source code for Grok Build, its command-line assistant that helps developers write and edit software.

title: A New Yardstick for How Human Voice Assistants Actually Sound
summary: Hugging Face released Real World VoiceEQ, a test that measures how natural and human a voice AI feels to real people, not just whether it gets the words right.

title: A Full Firefox Web Browser Now Runs Inside a Web Page
summary: Developers got the Firefox browser running entirely inside another browser tab, using a technology called WebAssembly that lets heavy desktop software run on a web page.

title: Running a Modern AI Model on a 13-Year-Old Server, No GPU
summary: A tinkerer got Gemma 4 26B — a sizeable open model from Google — generating text at about 5 words per second on a 2013-era Xeon server with no graphics card, relying only on ordinary system memory and a lot of careful tuning.

title: Why Automatically Routing Requests to Cheaper AI Models Is Harder Than It Looks
summary: IBM researchers, writing on Hugging Face, walked through why a seemingly simple idea — send easy questions to a cheap AI model and hard ones to an expensive model — keeps tripping teams up.

title: Hugging Face Catches an AI-Driven Break-In
summary: Hugging Face, the company that hosts much of the world's open AI models, disclosed that attackers broke into part of its production systems — and that this intrusion was driven by AI acting on its own, moving faster than the human attacks the team had handled before.

title: A New Free AI Model Claims Frontier-Level Smarts: Kimi K3
summary: The team behind Kimi released K3, an open model they describe as 'frontier intelligence' — meaning it aims to match the quality of the paid systems from OpenAI and Google, while being free to download and run.

title: Google Folds NotebookLM Into Gemini
summary: Google is renaming NotebookLM — its popular tool for turning your own documents into summaries, study guides, and audio overviews — to 'Gemini Notebook,' bringing it under the same brand as its main AI assistant.

title: LM Studio Adds an AI 'Agent' for Models You Run Yourself
summary: LM Studio, an app that lets people run AI models on their own computer, launched Bionic — an agent that can carry out multi-step tasks using those local models rather than a cloud service.

title: NVIDIA's New Retrieval Model Tops the RTEB Leaderboard
summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Embed, an 'embedding' model — the piece that helps AI find the right document to answer a question — and it now ranks first overall on RTEB, a public benchmark for retrieval quality.

title: Scaling 'Zero' Reinforcement Learning to a Trillion Parameters
summary: Researchers behind Ring-Zero describe training a one-trillion-parameter model using reinforcement learning from scratch — 'zero RL,' meaning the model learns to reason by trial and error rather than by copying human-written examples.
